people.name: Gavin Newsom
people.niche: Governor of California (D), state AI regulation
people.reason: As governor of the state that hosts most frontier AI labs, he vetoed SB 1047, signed SB 53, and issued AI executive orders on state use of AI and on worker displacement, so his decisions set de facto US AI policy.
people.gap: The map has no executive-branch, pro-innovation 'balanced guardrails' voice that regulates AI while openly rejecting compute-threshold safety regimes and outright bans for minors.
people.flag: Review: in June 2026 the governor's office announced a partnership supplying Anthropic tools to California state agencies (gov.ca.gov, 2026-06-29). Anthropic makes the model doing this research.

people.name: Scott Wiener
people.niche: California state senator (D-San Francisco), author of SB 1047 and SB 53
people.reason: He wrote the two most contested US frontier-AI safety bills and frames catastrophic-risk regulation as a progressive check on corporate self-regulation.
people.gap: Without him the map lacks the elected-legislator safety-hawk position: binding pre-deployment testing, kill switches and whistleblower protection, held against both industry and parts of his own party.
people.flag: Review: Anthropic engaged on SB 1047 (his own release names Anthropic as a group that helped refine the bill) and publicly backed SB 53. He was also a 2026 congressional candidate (CA-11), so recent statements are campaign-adjacent.

people.name: Andrew Yang
people.niche: Former presidential candidate, Forward Party co-founder, UBI and automation advocate
people.reason: He has argued since 2019 that automation and AI will displace millions of workers and that a universal basic income funded by AI-driven profits is necessary.
people.gap: The map lacks a centrist, non-partisan, labour-displacement-first voice whose main remedy is cash redistribution rather than safety regulation.

people.name: Pete Buttigieg
people.niche: Former US Transportation Secretary (D), likely 2028 contender
people.reason: He argues that Democrats and the public are 'profoundly underreacting' to AI, and frames its effect on jobs, wealth concentration and belonging as a policy choice rather than a technology puzzle.
people.gap: The map lacks a mainstream Democratic national-politician voice that treats AI as the central social-contract issue of the next election cycle.
people.flag: Only 3 usable works found. His Substack has a single AI essay; the other two are labelled interview transcripts.

people.name: Barack Obama
people.reason: Over a decade he has set out a consistent view: AI is transformative and unstoppable, but its gains must be shared through public oversight, guardrails, and possibly a shorter work week or guaranteed income.
people.gap: The map lacks the elder-statesman, institutionalist liberal view linking AI to democracy, disinformation and the distribution of economic gains.

works.author: gavin-newsom
works.title: SB 1047 veto message
works.channel: Office of the Governor of California
works.note: About 700 words, text-extractable PDF. Argues that compute and cost thresholds give a 'false sense of security' and that smaller models may be equally dangerous. Says regulation should rest on deployment risk and on an 'empirical trajectory analysis'. Says 'we cannot afford to wait for a major catastrophe', and that a California-only approach may be warranted absent federal action.

works.author: gavin-newsom
works.title: SB 53 (Transparency in Frontier AI Act) signing message
works.channel: Office of the Governor of California
works.note: About 450 words. Frames frontier-AI oversight as a model for the nation 'in the absence of a comprehensive federal AI policy framework', building on the expert working-group report. Wants alignment with any future federal standards that meet or exceed SB 53. CAVEAT: the PDF is an image-only scan with no text layer, so it needs OCR (tesseract output verified locally). The related gov.ca.gov press release carries only about 70 words from Newsom and is mostly other people's quotes, so it was left out.

works.author: gavin-newsom
works.title: AB 1064 (LEAD for Kids companion-chatbot bill) veto message
works.channel: Office of the Governor of California
works.note: About 450 words on children and AI. Supports safeguards for minors and cites SB 243's suicide-protocol and disclosure rules. Rejects a de facto ban: 'We cannot prepare our youth for a future where AI is ubiquitous by preventing their use of these tools altogether.' Calls for AI literacy. CAVEAT: the PDF is an image-only scan, so it needs OCR. The OCR reads the date stamp as 'OCT 18'; press coverage dates the veto to Oct 13, 2025.

works.author: gavin-newsom
works.title: Executive Order N-12-23 on generative AI
works.channel: Office of the Governor of California
works.note: About 2,500 words, text PDF. Formal executive order (format tagged 'letter' as the nearest enum value), with WHEREAS clauses giving his positions: GenAI as a leap for medicine and climate, California leadership, a 'new generation of risks', equity for marginalized communities. Directs risk reports and procurement guidance. Legalistic register.

works.author: gavin-newsom
works.title: Executive Order N-6-26 on AI and workforce disruption
works.channel: Office of the Governor of California
works.note: About 2,700 words, text PDF. Formal executive order (format tagged 'letter') preparing for AI job displacement. Has agencies study severance standards, unemployment-insurance and transition support, worker ownership, 'universal basic capital', retraining and WARN Act updates. Shows his shift toward labour-impact policy. Legalistic register.

works.author: scott-wiener
works.title: Senator Wiener Responds to OpenAI Opposition to SB 1047
works.note: About 500 words of his own statement. Rebuts the leave-it-to-Congress, national-security and companies-will-leave arguments. Calls pre-release catastrophic-risk testing and shutdown capability 'reasonable and implementable'. Ends with endorsements from national-security figures (other people's words). Names Anthropic among groups that helped refine the bill.

works.author: scott-wiener
works.title: Senator Wiener Responds to Speaker Emerita Pelosi's Opposition to SB 1047
works.note: About 600 words, nearly all his own statement. Says innovation and safety are not mutually exclusive and that 'pure industry self-regulation doesn't work out well for society'. Describes SB 1047 as a light-touch bill building on Biden's executive order, and cites Hinton, Bengio, Lessig and Russell. Shows an intra-party split.

works.author: scott-wiener
works.title: Senator Wiener Responds to Governor Newsom Vetoing Landmark AI Bill
works.note: About 550 words of his own statement. Says voluntary industry commitments 'are not enforceable', criticizes Congress's 'continuing paralysis', and calls the claim that the bill lacks empirical basis 'patently absurd'. Pairs directly with newsom-sb1047-veto. The second half of the page quotes Hinton and co-sponsors (CAIS Action Fund and others), so extract only his paragraphs.

works.author: scott-wiener
works.title: Senator Wiener Responds to Top Experts' Final Report on AI Governance Framework
works.note: About 350 words. Says AI promises 'abundance and broad-based prosperity' but needs guardrails 'with haste'. Opposes federal preemption that would 'wash away state protections' (deepfakes, algorithmic bias, IP). Bridge to SB 53. Short.

works.author: scott-wiener
works.title: Senator Wiener's Statement Supporting Governor Newsom's AI Kill Switch Executive Order
works.note: About 150 words of his own statement, so short. Urges acting 'with all possible haste' on AI-driven catastrophe and backs mandatory kill switches after the 2026 'rogue AI' incidents. Says 'California must not repeat the mistakes of Washington.' Most recent stance; campaign season.

works.author: andrew-yang
works.title: Surrounded on AI
works.note: About 900 words. Sets out four explicit theses: AI will accelerate inequality; it will cut jobs faster than it creates them; UBI will become necessary; the market optimizes for profit, not human dignity. Discusses white-collar and entry-level coding displacement. Ideal for proposition extraction.

works.author: andrew-yang
works.title: The Alignment Problem
works.note: About 1,100 words on AI risk and regulation. Sets out three principles: how to turn AI off, company accountability for harms, and reducing the chance of harm at scale. Asks who is liable when bots hack, argues IPO incentives push labs to 'plunge forward', and floats a slowdown. Mentions a researcher's warning after leaving Anthropic (context, not a conflict of interest).

works.author: andrew-yang
works.title: The Three Words No One Wants to Hear
works.note: About 800 words. Says 'with the help of AI, capital displaces labor' (a line he quotes from a CEO and endorses), and covers the collapsing entry-level job market for graduates, the economics of degree debt, and a negative income tax funded by AI profits. Reaffirms his 2019 prediction that coders would be automated.

works.author: andrew-yang
works.title: Labor on the Run
works.note: About 800 words, Labor Day piece. Says AI spending will push labour's share of GDP below 50% and that capitalism is becoming 'unduly harsh'. Discusses union decline, graduate underemployment, and redistribution. Quotes Dalio, Benioff and Buffett briefly.

works.author: andrew-yang
works.title: The Dominos are Falling
works.note: About 650 words. Reacts to reported Microsoft buyouts of 60,000 staff as operations shift to AI, and argues large-scale white-collar displacement has begun. Short. All five Yang works are 2026 Substack posts; I found no older bylined op-ed before the search budget ran out.

works.author: pete-buttigieg
works.title: We Are Still Underreacting on AI
works.note: Full essay, about 1,200 words. Says America and the Democratic Party are 'profoundly underreacting' and 'dangerously underprepared'. Compares AI to the Enlightenment and the Industrial Revolution. Concerns: wealth and poverty, work, citizenship and power, isolation and belonging. Says no technology is inherently good or bad, so the question is who decides.

works.author: pete-buttigieg
works.title: Pete Buttigieg has a warning about AI (NPR interview excerpt)
works.channel: Differ We Must (Steve Inskeep's Substack), from NPR Morning Edition
works.note: Interviewer's own Substack reproducing the AI portion of his July 2025 NPR interview, with speakers labelled (BUTTIGIEG:/INSKEEP:). Says Democrats risk 'fighting the last war' and that 'half of the entry level jobs might not be there' in three or four years. Intro paragraphs are Inskeep's words, and the text is 'edited slightly'. The full NPR transcript (npr.org/transcripts/nx-s1-5475197) mentions AI only in passing.

works.author: pete-buttigieg
works.title: The New American Era: An Interview with Pete Buttigieg
works.note: Q&A with speakers labelled (HPR:/PB:), edited for length. The AI answer is about 250 words: he expects disruption at least on the scale of the industrial Midwest. Good outcome: 'a shorter work week and more money in your pocket'. Bad outcome: higher concentrations of wealth and power. 'Not a technology puzzle; it's a policy question.' The rest covers affordability and the Democratic coalition.

works.author: barack-obama
works.title: Barack Obama, Neural Nets, Self-Driving Cars, and the Future of the World
works.note: Long conversation (about 4,500 words) with Joi Ito and Scott Dadich, speakers labelled (Obama:/Ito:/Dadich:). Covers general vs specialized AI, government funding of basic research, wage suppression and inequality, rethinking the social compact, and diversity in who builds AI. Joi Ito speaks at length, so extract only Obama's turns. Older work, but it establishes his long-held view.

works.author: barack-obama
works.title: Barack Obama on AI, free speech, and the future of the internet
works.note: Full transcript, about 7,000 words. Recorded the week of Biden's AI executive order. Topics: guardrails without anti-tech panic, frontier-system transparency, smallpox and critical-infrastructure risks, children, lessons from failing to regulate social media, the First Amendment, and experts serving in government. CAVEAT: speakers are not name-labelled; Patel's turns are in <strong> bold and Obama's are plain, so separate them by markup. Plain GET returns 200; WebFetch is blocked for this site.

works.author: barack-obama
works.title: President Obama's remarks at the 2023 Democracy Forum
works.note: Prepared remarks, about 6,500 words, on inclusive economic growth. The AI passage (about 400 words) says automation is replacing blue- and soon white-collar jobs, that disruptive technology 'is not going away', and that AI benefits must 'flow to everyone' under public debate and safety review. He backs Biden-era regulation and slowing the rollout of untested powerful models. Elsewhere he discusses worker power, shorter work weeks and guaranteed income. Date inferred from the forum date (Nov 2023); the page has no date stamp.

works.author: barack-obama
works.title: Obama Speaks at Hamilton College (conversation with Steven Tepper)
works.channel: Hamilton College Sacerdote Great Names Series (transcript by Rev)
works.note: Timestamped transcript with speakers labelled (Barack Obama/Steven Tepper). The AI segment (about 50:00 to 56:00) says AI 'will be more impactful' than social media and come faster, that current models code better than '60, 70% of coders', that routine white-collar work will go, and that the big questions are about meaning, distribution and the value of a liberal-arts education. The rest of the conversation covers democracy and the political climate. Rev posted the transcript on 2025-04-09.
